finding: Pinned-source inspection refines worker198: Peer<RoleClient>::call_tool_once itself still shows no explicit local precondition requiring the client to advertise the tasks extension before sending tools/call, and it accepts ServerResult::CreateTaskResult as CallToolResponse::Task. However, the same commit has an explicit server-side dispatch guard in ServerHandler::handle_request for ClientRequest::CallToolRequest: after call_tool returns, any CallToolResponse::Task is rejected with Missing Required Client Capability when the request/session client capabilities do not declare tasks. The pinned end-to-end test dispatch_rejects_task_result_for_non_declaring_client exercises this failure path with a deliberately misbehaving handler and expects -32021. Thus task capability enforcement exists, but in the inspected path it is server-dispatch enforcement rather than a caller-side call_tool_once precondition.
